translations.text: In the eighth month, on the first day of the month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the Lord came to the prophet Zechariah, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, saying:
The Lord was very angry with your ancestors.
Tell them: This is what the Lord Almighty says: Return to me, says the Lord Almighty, and I will return to you, says the Lord Almighty.

Do not be like your ancestors, to whom the earlier prophets proclaimed: This is what the Lord Almighty says: Turn from your evil ways and your evil deeds. But they did not listen or pay attention to me, says the Lord.
Where are your ancestors? And do my prophets live forever?

But your ancestors remembered my words and the commands that I gave to my servants the prophets. They reflected and said, “Just as the Lord Almighty intended to deal with us according to our ways and our deeds, so he has dealt with us.”
On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of the Lord came to the prophet Zechariah, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, saying:
At night I saw a man riding a red horse, standing among the shade trees. Behind him were red, dappled, and white horses.
I said, “What are these, my lord?” The angel who was speaking with me answered me, “I will show you what these are.”
The man standing among the trees answered me, “These are the ones the Lord has sent to walk throughout the earth.”
They answered the angel of the Lord who was standing among the trees, “We have walked throughout the earth, and the whole earth is settled and quiet.”
The angel of the Lord answered, “Lord Almighty, how long will you withhold mercy from Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, with which you have been angry these seventy years?”
The Lord answered the angel who was speaking with me with kind words and comforting messages.
The angel who was speaking with me said to me, “Proclaim: This is what the Lord Almighty says: I am deeply jealous for Jerusalem and Zion.
I am very angry with the nations that are in turmoil, for I was only a little angry, but they made the disaster worse.”

Therefore, this is what the Lord Almighty says: “I have returned to Jerusalem with compassion, and I will place my house within it,” says the Lord Almighty. “A measuring line will be stretched over Jerusalem.”
Proclaim again and say, “This is what the Lord Almighty says: From now on the cities will be emptied of good things. The Lord will rebuild Zion and will again choose Jerusalem.”
I looked up and saw four horns.
I said to the angel who was speaking with me, “What are these, my lord?” He said to me, “These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.”
Then the Lord showed me four carpenters.

I said, “What have these come to do?” He said to me, “These are the horns that scattered Judah, like the mouth of a man [?] who did not lift his head. These have come to shake them and uproot the horns of the nations that raised their horn against the land of Judah to scatter it.”
I looked up and saw a man with a measuring line in his hand.
I said to him, “Where are you going?” He said to me, “To measure Jerusalem and see how long and how wide it is.”
The angel who was speaking with me went out, and another angel came to meet him.
He said to him, “Run and tell that young man: Jerusalem will be inhabited like open countryside because of the many people and livestock within it.
I myself will be within it, says the Lord, like a wall of fire, and I will be the glory within it.”
“Oh, oh! Flee from the land of the north, says the Lord, for I have scattered you to the four winds of heaven, says the Lord.
Oh, Zion, escape, you who live with the daughter of Babylon!”
For this is what the Lord Almighty says: “After glory he sent me against the nations that plunder you, for whoever touches you touches the pupil of his eye.”
“For look, I am raising my hand against them, and their servants will become plunder. Then you will know that the Lord Almighty sent me.”
“Sing praise and rejoice, daughter of Zion, for look, I am coming and will dwell among you,” says the Lord.
Many nations will join themselves to the Lord on that day and will become his people. He will dwell among you, and you will know that the Lord Almighty sent me to you.
The Lord will inherit Judah as his portion in his holy land, and he will choose Jerusalem again.
Let all humanity fear before the Lord, for he is awakening from his holy dwelling.
He showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord, with Satan standing at his right hand to harm him.
The angel of the Lord said to Satan, “Satan, may the Lord rebuke you! May the Lord who chose Jerusalem rebuke you! This is a burning stick rescued from the fire.”
Joshua was wearing filthy clothes and was standing before the angel of the Lord.

The angel spoke and said to those standing before him, “Remove his filthy clothes.” They removed his filthy clothes, and he said to him, “See, I have removed your guilt from you and clothed you in fine clothes.”
He said, “Let them put a clean crown on his head.” They put a clean crown on his head and dressed him in fine clothes, while the angel of the Lord stood there.
The angel of the Lord solemnly charged Joshua, saying:
“This is what the Lord Almighty says: If you walk in my ways and keep my commandments, you will govern my house and guard my courtyard. I will give you those who walk among these who stand here.”
“Listen, Joshua the high priest, you and your companions who stand before you, for you are men who serve as signs. Look, I am bringing my servant, the Dawn.”
“For look at the stone I have placed before Joshua: on this one stone are seven eyes. Look, I am opening its gates,” says the Lord Almighty, “and I will remove the guilt of that land on that day.”
“On that very day,” says the Lord Almighty, “each of you will invite his neighbor under the vine and under the fig tree.”
The angel who was speaking with me returned and awakened me, like someone awakened from sleep.
He said to me, “What have you seen?” I said, “I have seen a gold lampstand with a bowl on top of it and seven lamps on it, with seven spouts for each lamp on top of it.”
“There are two olive trees beside it, one to the right of the bowl and one to its left.”
I spoke and said to the angel who was speaking with me, “What are these, my lord?”
The angel who was speaking with me answered and said to me, “Do you not know what these are?” I said, “I do not know, my lord.”
He said to me, “This is the word of the Lord concerning Zerubbabel: ‘Not by might and not by strength, but by the Spirit,’ says the Lord Almighty.”
“What are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you are nothing but a plain. He will bring out the chief stone of equality and mercy.”
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
“Zerubbabel’s hands laid the foundations of this house, and his hands will complete it. Then you will know that the Lord Almighty sent me to you.”
“For who has despised the days of small things? They will look and see the plumb stone in Zerubbabel’s hands. These are the seven eyes of the Lord, which look throughout the whole earth.”
I spoke and said to him, “What are these two olive trees to the right of the bowl and to its left?”
I spoke a second time and said to him, “What are these two olive branches between the two gold spouts that pour gold out of themselves?”
He said to me, “Do you not know what these are?” I said, “No, my lord.”
He said to me, “These are the two anointed ones who stand before the Lord of the whole earth.”
I raised my eyes and saw a flying scroll.
He said to me, “What do you see?” I said, “I see a flying scroll, twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide.”

He said to me, “This is the curse that goes out over the face of the whole earth. For everyone who steals is acquitted by it according to its terms, and everyone who swears is acquitted by it according to its terms.”

“I will send it out,” says the Lord Almighty, “and it will enter the house of the thief and the house of everyone who swears falsely by my name. It will remain inside his house and consume its timber and its stones.”
The angel who was speaking with me came out and said to me, “Raise your eyes and see what this is that is coming out.”
I said, “What is it?” He said to me, “This is the measuring basket that is coming out, and in it are the sins of the whole earth.”
Then a talent of lead was lifted, and a woman was sitting inside the measuring basket.
He said to me, “This is Sin.” He threw her into the measuring basket and threw the lead weight over its opening.
I raised my eyes and saw two women coming out, with wind in their wings. They had wings like the wings of a stork, and they lifted the measuring basket between earth and heaven.
I said to the angel who was speaking with me, “Where are they taking the measuring basket?”
He said to me, “To build a house for it in the land of Babylon. They will prepare it and set it there on its base.”
Again I raised my eyes and saw four chariots coming out from between two mountains. Those mountains were mountains of bronze.
The first chariot had red horses, and the second chariot had black horses.
In the third chariot were white horses, and in the fourth chariot were dappled horses.
I said to the angel who was speaking with me, “What are these, my lord?”
The angel answered me, “These are the four winds of heaven, which were standing before the Lord of the whole earth.”
The black horses in it are going out to the northern land. The white horses are going out after them, and the dappled horses are going out to the southern land.
The red horses came out and sought to go and roam throughout the earth. He said to them, “Go, roam throughout the earth.” And they roamed throughout the earth.
He called out and said to me, “Look! Those going out to the northern land are bringing my spirit to rest in the northern land.”
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Take from the exiles—from Heldai, Tobiah, and Jedaiah—and come that same day and enter the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah, who came from Babylon.
Take his silver and gold, make a crown, and place it on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
Say to him, “This is what the Lord Almighty says: Look, a man whose name is Sunrise! From below he will rise.”
He will build the temple of the Lord, and he will receive glory. He will sit and rule on his throne, and there will be a priest on his throne. There will be peaceful counsel between the two of them.
The crown will belong to Heldai, Tobiah, Jedaiah, and Josiah son of Zephaniah as a memorial in the temple of the Lord.
Those who are far away will come and build the temple of the Lord. You will know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you, if you obey the voice of the Lord your God.
In the fourth year of King Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, which is Kanun.
He sent Sharezer and Rab-mag to Bethel, and the king and his warriors sent them to pray for him before the Lord.
And to say to the priests in the house of the Lord Almighty and to the prophets, “Should I weep in the fifth month or abstain, as I have done for so many years?”
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Say to all the people of the land and to the priests, “When you fasted and danced in the fifth and seventh months for these seventy years, was it really for me that you fasted?”
And when you eat and drink, is it not you who eat and drink?
These are the words that the Lord proclaimed through the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at peace, with towns surrounding it, and the mountains and plains were inhabited.
And the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, saying:
This is what the Lord Almighty says: Judge with true justice, and show kindness and mercy to one another.
Do not abuse or oppress widows, orphans, the poor, or anyone who turns to me. Do not plot evil in your hearts against one another.
But they refused to listen to me. They stubbornly turned their shoulders away and stopped their ears so that they would not hear.

They made their hearts like flint so that they would not hear the laws and commandments that the Lord Almighty sent by his Spirit through the earlier prophets. So great anger came from the Lord Almighty.
Just as I called them and they did not listen, so they will call me and I will not listen to them, says the Lord Almighty.

I will scatter them among all the nations they have not known, and the land will become desolate after them, with no one passing through or returning, because they made the desirable land a wasteland.
And the word of the Lord Almighty came to me, saying:
This is what the Lord Almighty says: I am intensely jealous for Zion; with great fury I am jealous for her.
This is what the Lord says: I take comfort in Zion, and I dwell within Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be called the holy city, and the mountain of the Lord Almighty will be called the holy mountain.
This is what the Lord Almighty says: Once again old men and old women will sit in the streets of Jerusalem, each holding a staff in hand because of advanced age.
The streets of the city will be filled with boys and girls playing in its streets.
This is what the Lord Almighty says: If this seems extraordinary to the remnant of this people in those days, will it also seem extraordinary to me? says the Lord Almighty.
This is what the Lord Almighty says: Look, I am saving my people from the land of the east and from the land of the setting sun.
I will bring them back, and they will dwell in Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God in truth and righteousness.

This is what the Lord Almighty says: Let the hands of all who heard these words in those days from the mouths of the prophets be strong, from the day when the foundation of the temple of the Lord Almighty was laid for it to be built.

For before those days and before that time, there were no wages for people or for animals, and there was no peace for anyone going out or coming in because of the oppressor. And look, I am setting all people against one another.
From now on I will not treat the remnant of this people as I did in earlier days, says the Lord Almighty.

For the seed will grow in peace, the vine will give its fruit, the earth will give its produce, and the heavens will give their dew. I will give the remnant of this people all these things as their inheritance.
Just as you, the house of Judah and the house of Israel, have been a curse among the nations, so I will save you, and you will become a blessing. Let your hands be strong, and do not be afraid.
For this is what the Lord Almighty says: Just as I planned to bring harm upon you when your ancestors angered me, says the Lord Almighty, and I did not turn back,
so I have turned and planned in these days to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Do not be afraid.
Do these things: Speak the truth to one another, and in your deliberations render judgments of truth, justice, and peace.
Do not plot evil in your hearts against one another, and do not love false oaths, for I hate all these things, says the Lord Almighty.
The word of the Lord Almighty came to me, saying:

This is what the Lord Almighty says: The fast of the fourth month, the fast of the fifth month, the fast of the seventh month, and the fast of the tenth month will become occasions of rejoicing, gladness, and pleasant festivals for the house of Judah. Love truth and peace.
This is what the Lord Almighty says: From now on, peoples and the inhabitants of many cities will come.
The inhabitants of one city will go to another and say, “Come, let us go and pray before the Lord and seek the Lord Almighty. I too will go.”
Many peoples and mighty nations will come to seek the Lord Almighty in Jerusalem and to pray before the Lord.

This is what the Lord Almighty says: In those days, ten men from all the languages of the nations will take hold of the hem of a Jewish man's garment and say to him, “Let us go with you, because we have heard that God is with you.”
The word of the Lord concerning the land of Hadrach, with Damascus as its offering, because human beings and all the tribes of Israel are visible to the Lord.
Hamath also will border on it, as will Tyre and Sidon, which have become very wise.
Tyre built herself a fortress and piled up silver like dust and gold like the mud of the street.
Therefore the Lord will destroy her and throw her wealth into the sea, and she will be consumed by fire.
Ashkelon will see and be afraid. Gaza will suffer greatly, and so will Ekron, because its hope has disappointed it. The king will perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon will be uninhabited.
Foreigners will live in Ashdod, and I will destroy the pride of the Philistines.
I will remove their blood from their mouths and their filth from between their teeth. They too will remain for our God and become like the leaders of Judah, and Ekron will be like Ebron.
I will station a guard over my house against those who pass by and those who return. No oppressor will pass over them again, because now I have seen with my own eyes.
Rejoice greatly, daughter Zion! Shout, daughter Jerusalem! Look, your king is coming to you, righteous, a savior, and humble, riding on a donkey, on a colt, the offspring of a female donkey.

He will destroy the chariots from Ephraim and the horses from Jerusalem. He will break the bow in battle and speak peace with the nations. He will rule from sea to sea and from the River to the ends of the earth.
You too, by the blood of your covenant, have released the prisoners from the pit that has no water in it.
Return to the stronghold, prisoners of the assembly. In return for one day, I will repay you two.
For I have drawn my bow over Judah and filled it over Ephraim. I have sent your sons, Zion, against your sons, Greece, and made you like a warrior's sword.
The Lord will appear over them, and his arrow will go out like lightning. The Lord of lords will sound the horn and go in a whirlwind toward the south.
The Lord Almighty will shield them. They will eat and subdue stones with a sling. They will drink turbid liquid like wine and be filled like a bowl and like the corners of the altar.
The Lord their God will save them on that day, his people like a flock, because they are holy stones scattered in his land.
How good and how beautiful! Grain is for the troops, and wine makes the young women glad.
Ask the Lord for rain in the season of the late rains. The Lord makes showers, and he will give you the early rain so that grass may grow in the open country.

For the soothsayers have spoken wickedness, and the diviners have seen lies. They have told false dreams and offered empty comfort. Therefore the people have wandered like sheep and have been brought low because they have no shepherd.
My anger has burned against the shepherds, and I will punish the male goats. For the Lord Almighty has attended to his flock, the house of Judah, and made them like a splendid horse in battle.
From them will come the cornerstone, from them the tent peg, from them the battle bow, and from them all their rulers will come forth together.
They will be like men trampling mud in the streets in battle. They will fight because the Lord is with them, and the horsemen will be put to shame.

I will strengthen the house of Judah and save the house of Joseph. I will bring them back because I have compassion on them. They will be as though I had not forgotten them, because I am the Lord God, and I will answer them.
They will be like the warriors of Ephraim, and their hearts will rejoice as though from wine. Their children will see and rejoice, and their hearts will delight in the Lord.
I will whistle for them and gather them, because I am redeeming them. They will become as numerous as they once were.
I will sow them among the nations, and in distant lands they will praise me. They will provide for their children and return.
I will bring them back from the land of Egypt and gather them from Assyria. I will bring them to the land of Gilead and to Lebanon, and there will not be enough room for them.

Distress will pass through the sea and turn back the waves in the sea. All the depths of the river will be put to shame. The pride of the Assyrians will cease, and the rule of the Egyptians will pass away.
I will strengthen them in the Lord, and they will put their hope in his name, says the Lord.
Open your gates, Lebanon, so that fire may consume your cedars!
Let the cypress wail, because the cedar has fallen and the mighty trees have been plundered. Let the oaks of Bashan wail, because the mighty forest has fallen.
The sound of shepherds wailing, because their splendor has been plundered! The sound of lions roaring, because the strength of the Jordan has been plundered!
This is what the Lord my God says: Shepherd the lean sheep.
Their buyers kill them and are not held guilty. Their sellers say, “Blessed is the Lord, for we have become rich!” Their shepherds have no pity on them.

For I will no longer have pity on the inhabitants of the land, says the Lord. Look, I am handing people over, each into the hands of his neighbor and into the hands of his king. They will divide up the land, and I will not rescue it from their hands.
I shepherded the lean sheep for the sake of the flock. I took two staffs for myself; one I named Pleasantness, and the other Cord. And I shepherded the sheep.
I destroyed three shepherds in one month. I grew weary of them, and they too howled against me.
I said, “I will not shepherd you. Let those that are dying die, and let those that are perishing perish. Let those that remain eat one another’s flesh.”
I took my staff Pleasantness and broke it, to annul the covenant I had made with all the peoples.
It was annulled that very day, and the humble among the sheep who were watching me knew that this was the word of the Lord.
I said to them, “If it seems right to you, give me my wages; otherwise you are cheating me.” And they weighed out thirty pieces of silver as my wages.
The Lord said to me, “Throw it into the treasury—the glorious price at which they valued me!” So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them into the treasury in the house of the Lord.
I broke Cord, my other staff, to dissolve the unity that existed between Judah and Israel.
The Lord said to me, “Once again, take for yourself the equipment of a foolish shepherd.

For look, I am raising up a shepherd in the land who will not attend to the perishing, seek the lost, bind up the injured, heal the sick, or feed those still standing. Instead, he will eat the flesh of the fat sheep and tear off their hooves.”
O foolish shepherd who abandoned the sheep! [?] against your arm and against your right eye! May your right arm wither and your right eye go blind!
The vision of the words of the Lord concerning Israel. The Lord says, who stretched out the heavens, established the foundations of the earth, and created the human spirit within a person:
Look, I am making Jerusalem a gateway of staggering for all the peoples surrounding it. Distress will also come upon Judah along with Jerusalem.
On that day I will make Jerusalem a threshing stone for all the peoples. All who trample it will surely be cut, and all the peoples of the earth will gather against it.

“On that day,” says the Lord, “I will strike all their horses with bewilderment and their riders with madness. I will open my eyes over the house of Judah, and I will strike all the horses of the peoples with blindness.”
The leaders of Judah will say in their hearts, “The inhabitants of Jerusalem have become stronger than we are through the Lord Almighty, their God.”

On that day I will make the leaders of Judah like a burning coal among wood and like a flaming torch among sheaves. They will consume all the peoples surrounding them, to the right and to the left, and Jerusalem will again be inhabited in its own place, in Jerusalem.
The Lord will attend to the tent of Judah as before, so that the glory of the house of David and the glory of Jerusalem’s inhabitants will not exceed that of the house of Judah.

On that day the Lord will shield the inhabitants of Jerusalem. On that day the weak among them will be like David, and the house of David will be like God, like the angel of the Lord going before them.
On that day I will seek to destroy all the peoples who come against Jerusalem.

I will pour out upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of compassion and mercy. They will look toward me concerning the one they pierced, and they will mourn for him as people mourn for an only child. They will grieve bitterly for him as people grieve for a firstborn.
On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be great, like the mourning for the son of Amon in the plain of Megiddo.
The land will mourn, clan by clan, each separately: the clan of the house of David by itself, and their wives by themselves; the clan of the house of Nathan by itself, and their wives by themselves;
the clan of the house of Simeon by itself, and their wives by themselves.
All the remaining clans will mourn, clan by clan, each by itself, and their wives by themselves.
On that day a fountain will be opened for the house of David and for the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for sprinkling and purification.
On that day, says the Lord Almighty, I will destroy the names of the idols from the land, and they will no longer be remembered. I will remove the false prophets and the unclean spirit from the land.

If a man prophesies again, his father and mother will say to him, “You must not live, because you have spoken lies in the Lord’s name.” His father and mother, who gave him birth, will bind him when he prophesies.
On that day the false prophets will each be ashamed of the vision of their prophecy. They will not wrap themselves in a hairy skin, because they have lied.
He will say, “I am not a prophet. I am a man who works the land, and a man put me to work from my youth.”
They will say to him, “What are these wounds on your hands?” He will say, “These are wounds I received in the house of my friends.”
Sword, awake against my shepherd, against the man who is my friend, says the Lord Almighty. Strike the shepherd, and his flock will scatter. I will turn my hand against the little ones.
Throughout the whole land, says the Lord, two parts of those in it will come to an end and perish, and a third will remain in it.

I will bring the third that remains into the fire. I will refine them as silver is refined and test them as gold is tested. They will call on my name, and I will answer them. I will say, “This is my people,” and they will say, “The Lord is my God.”
Look, the day of the Lord is coming, and the plunder taken from you will be divided within you.

I will gather all the peoples against Jerusalem for battle. The city will be captured, the houses plundered, and the women raped. Half the city will go into captivity, but half the people will not perish from the city.
The Lord will go out and fight against those nations, as he fought on the day of battle.

His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, which faces Jerusalem on its eastern side. The Mount of Olives will split, half toward the east and half toward the west, and there will be a very great valley in it. Half the mountain will be left to the north and half to the south.

You will flee to the valley of the mountain, because the valley of the mountains will reach to the place of distress. You will flee as you fled from the earthquake that occurred in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. The Lord my God will come in, and all his holy ones with him.
On that day there will be no light, but cold and ice.
There will be one day, and that day will be known to the Lord, neither night nor day. At evening there will be light.
On that day living water will flow out from Jerusalem, half toward the eastern sea and half toward the western sea, in summer and winter.
The Lord will be king over the whole earth. On that day the Lord will be one, and his name one.

He will turn the whole land into a plain, from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be raised up and remain in its place, from the Benjamin Gate to the site of the former gate, as far as the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king’s winepress.
People will live in it, and there will no longer be a curse of destruction. Jerusalem will dwell in peace.

This will be the plague with which the Lord strikes all the peoples who fight against Jerusalem: their flesh will waste away while they are standing on their feet, their eyes will waste away in their sockets, and their tongues will waste away in their mouths.
On that day a great panic from the Lord will fall upon them. Each will seize his companion, and his hand will cling to his companion’s hand.
Judah too will fight in Jerusalem, and the wealth of all the surrounding peoples will be gathered: gold, silver, and clothing in great abundance.
The same plague will fall on the horses, mules, camels, donkeys, and all the livestock in these camps, just like this plague.
Everyone who remains from all the peoples who came against Jerusalem will go up year after year to worship the King, the Lord Almighty, and to celebrate the Festival of Shelters.
If any of the families of the earth do not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord Almighty, no rain will fall on them.
If the people of Egypt do not go up and do not come, they too will suffer the plague with which the Lord will strike the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Booths.
This will be the punishment for Egypt and the punishment for all the peoples who do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Shelters.
On that day, “Holy to the Lord” will be on the bridles of the horses. The cooking pots in the Lord’s house will be like the bowls before the altar.

Every cooking pot in Judah and Jerusalem will be holy to the Lord Almighty. All who offer sacrifices will come and take some of them and cook in them. On that day there will no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the Lord Almighty.
